messages:
morgan: Heads up — noticed a tail latency bump on SSE endpoints after yesterday's merge. p50 unchanged, p95 ~ +40ms, p99 jumping ~200ms. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/s/streams/latency :thinking_face:

sam: saw the CI perf alert too. test suite flagged `streaming-integration` flaky on `merge/feature/proto-chunking` at 11:12pm. cc @kevin

ci-bot: CI: streaming-integration perf test failed on commit 0a3f7d5 — p99 increased by 180ms vs baseline. Artifacts: /artifacts/0a3f7d5/streaming-perf.log

kevin: quick summary from flamegraph: time moved from kernel selection + small serialization -> more time spent in `sse_writer.flush()` path where we now coalesce tiny frames. Looks like `linger` behavior + new prefill scheduling changed when KV-prefetch fires. KV cache hit rate dropped concurrently (92% -> 71%).

morgan: interesting — KV hit drop could amplify p99 since more backend calls and different kernel choice for longer sequences. any repro?

sam: repro with this script gives visible gap:

```bash
# reproduce SSE drip
python tools/repro_sse.py --model small --stream-delay 12 --toolcall true
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' https://api.redwood.test/stream
```

kevin: repro logs attached in artifacts show batches of 1 tokens frequently after merge, kernel auto-select picks generic slow kernel instead of short-seq optimized one. Batching heuristic now defers prefill until KV-pop, which is the regression vector.

morgan: can we bisect to the exact commit? sam — can you run a git-bisect on the release branch? if it's the framing change we should hold the rollout.

sam: started bisect, narrowed to 0a3f7d5 -> 0a3f7d5^ (the framing refactor). The refactor reduced number of small writes but introduced a logic path that delays KV-prefetch until `frame_end` event. Patch attached in PR #4231.

kevin: suggested fix: trigger KV-prefetch on first token of a stream rather than `frame_end`. Also tweak batching heuristic to prefer short-seq kernel if average batch size < 4. I pushed a prototype to `kevin/stream-prefetch-fix`.
buildbot: Rolling canary hold placed on `edge/streaming` since 2026-02-18T03:00Z due to latency regression. Revert candidate: revert commit 0a3f7d5.

morgan: applied revert in canary, running 30k synthetic streams. Early results: p99 back down ~160ms from the spike, KV-hit returned to ~90%. Good sign. But noticed toolcall serialization still ~10ms higher vs baseline.

kevin: that extra ~10ms is likely from the new framing encode path (less memcpy but more small allocations). I have a micro-optimizing patch to reuse buffers in the serializer. Will run perf CI.
dana: opened tracking ticket PROJ-1987 for follow-up: persistent toolcall serialization delta + add a regression test in perf CI for SSE p99. Please link the bisect notes and artifacts.

morgan: thanks all — holding rollout until kevin's serializer patch lands and perf CI is green. If anyone finds additional repros (esp with toolcall heavy flows), drop them here. :thumbsup:
